text: When you build a REST API, good design matters. Start by giving your endpoints clear, simple names that show what they do. Use the right HTTP methods, like GET to read data and POST to create it. Always return proper status codes so clients know what happened — for example, 200 for success and 404 when something is missing. Write clear documentation so other developers can understand and use your API easily. Finally, plan for versioning from the beginning. This lets you improve your API without breaking existing apps. Following these basic rules makes your API easier to use, maintain, and trust.
